vars.label: Toxics Release Inventory facilities (EPA)
vars.ref: EPA TRI Basic Data File, Puerto Rico, reporting year 2024
vars.definition: Facilities that filed a Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) report with EPA for 2024: plants of covered industries that make, process or otherwise use more than a threshold amount of a listed toxic chemical. A count of facilities, not of releases or of their amounts. Counted in the barrio whose outline holds the site's point (a coastal site within 2 km of one counts there); a municipio is the sum of its barrios.

vars.label: Risk Management Plan facilities (EPA)
vars.ref: EPA Facility Registry Service, RMP interests marked active, read 2026-10-17
vars.definition: Facilities with an active Risk Management Plan (RMP) registration in EPA's Facility Registry Service: places that hold more than a threshold quantity of a listed toxic or flammable substance (water and wastewater plants, chemical, energy and food plants, among others). Counted in the barrio whose outline holds the site's point (a coastal site within 2 km of one counts there); a municipio is the sum of its barrios.

vars.label: Superfund National Priorities List sites (EPA)
vars.ref: EPA Facility Registry Service, SEMS_NPL layer, currently on the final NPL, read 2026-10-17
vars.definition: Superfund sites currently on EPA's final National Priorities List, as EPA's Facility Registry Service places them: hazardous waste sites EPA ranks for long-term cleanup. Sites deleted from the list are not counted. Counted in the barrio whose outline holds the site's point (a coastal site within 2 km of one counts there); a municipio is the sum of its barrios.

vars.label: Municipal solid waste landfills, open or closed (EPA LMOP)
vars.ref: EPA LMOP landfills with coordinates, data edited 2024-09-20
vars.definition: Municipal solid waste landfills in EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program database, open or closed. LMOP does not list every landfill, and lists no open dumps, transfer stations, industrial or hazardous waste landfills. Counted in the barrio whose outline holds the site's point (a coastal site within 2 km of one counts there); a municipio is the sum of its barrios.

vars.label: Municipal solid waste landfills still open (EPA LMOP)
vars.ref: EPA LMOP landfills with coordinates, data edited 2024-09-20
vars.definition: Municipal solid waste landfills that EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program lists as open (accepting waste). The status is LMOP's as of its last update, which can lag a closure. Counted in the barrio whose outline holds the site's point (a coastal site within 2 km of one counts there); a municipio is the sum of its barrios.

vars.label: Area draining to or in a 303(d)-listed impaired water (EPA ATTAINS, %)
vars.ref: EPA ATTAINS assessment units, Puerto Rico, 2024 reporting cycle
vars.definition: The share of the area inside an assessment unit that Puerto Rico's water quality report puts on the Clean Water Act 303(d) list (impaired, and a cleanup plan still needed). Puerto Rico maps its rivers and streams as the land that drains to each assessed reach, so a listed unit covers that watershed; lakes, estuaries and coastal waters are their own areas. A barrio touches a listed water when its share is above 0.

vars.label: Area in a sulfur dioxide non-attainment area (EPA Green Book, %)
vars.ref: EPA Green Book non-attainment areas, current status read 2026-10-17
vars.definition: The share of the area inside an area that EPA designates as not meeting the 1-hour sulfur dioxide standard of 2010 (non-attainment), as EPA's Green Book maps it. A barrio is in a non-attainment area when its share is above 0. It says where the designation applies, not what anyone breathes.

vars.label: Area in a lead non-attainment area (EPA Green Book, %)
vars.ref: EPA Green Book non-attainment areas, current status read 2026-10-17
vars.definition: The share of the area inside an area that EPA designates as not meeting the lead standard of 2008 (non-attainment), as EPA's Green Book maps it. A barrio is in a non-attainment area when its share is above 0. It says where the designation applies, not what anyone breathes.

vars.label: Households with one or more severe housing problems (HUD CHAS)
vars.ref: HUD CHAS 2016-2020, census tracts (Table 2), from HUD eGIS
vars.definition: Households with at least one of the four severe housing problems in HUD's CHAS data (2016-2020): a home without complete kitchen facilities, without complete plumbing, with more than 1.5 people per room, or a household paying more than half of its income for housing. The barrio values are estimates: each tract's counts are spread over its barrios in proportion to the 2020 housing units each barrio has in the tract (docs/geography.md, section 4), so a barrio that lies in several tracts gets a blend of them. The municipio values are exact sums of their tracts.

vars.label: Households with one or more severe housing problems (HUD CHAS, %)
vars.ref: HUD CHAS 2016-2020, census tracts (Table 2), from HUD eGIS
vars.definition: The share of households with at least one of the four severe housing problems in HUD's CHAS data (2016-2020): no complete kitchen, no complete plumbing, more than 1.5 people per room, or housing costs above half of income. The barrio values are estimates: each tract's counts are spread over its barrios in proportion to the 2020 housing units each barrio has in the tract (docs/geography.md, section 4), so a barrio that lies in several tracts gets a blend of them. The municipio values are exact sums of their tracts.

vars.label: Street intersections (TIGER/Line)
vars.ref: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES, 78 municipios
vars.definition: Street intersections: points where three or more street segments of the Census Bureau's TIGER/Line 2026 files meet (secondary roads, local streets, alleys and private roads; limited-access highways, ramps, service drives, trails, walkways and parking lot roads are left out). A dead end or a bend is not an intersection. Counted in the barrio that holds each point.

vars.label: Street intersections per square mile (TIGER/Line)
vars.ref: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES; 2020 Census land area
vars.definition: Street intersections: points where three or more street segments of the Census Bureau's TIGER/Line 2026 files meet (secondary roads, local streets, alleys and private roads; limited-access highways, ramps, service drives, trails, walkways and parking lot roads are left out). A dead end or a bend is not an intersection. Divided by the land area in square miles (2020 Census). Higher means a finer street grid, usually easier to walk.

vars.group: Health care · Distance to a general hospital
vars.label: Drive time to the nearest general hospital (estimate, minutes)
vars.ref: Computed by the observatory from CMS's hospital list (each hospital placed at its OpenStreetMap building or HHS's geocoded address), the 2020 census blocks and OpenStreetMap roads (conditions.py)
vars.definition: From each barrio's population-weighted point (the 2020 census blocks of the barrio, weighted by their residents) to the nearest general acute care hospital with an emergency department in CMS's Hospital General Information list (37 of the 52 placed at their OpenStreetMap building, found by name or near HHS's geocoded address; 15 at HHS's geocoded address), along the observatory's OpenStreetMap road graph in either direction. A barrio that holds a hospital is 0. Which barrios are 0 is uncertain near the 15 hospitals placed at HHS's address: of the 27 hospitals found by name that HHS also places, HHS's point falls in another barrio for 13. A municipio's figure is the average of its barrios weighted by their 2020 residents. Vieques and Culebra have no road link to a hospital (a trip needs a ferry or a flight), so they have no value, and Puerto Rico's figure leaves out their residents. Other barrios with no value: Isla de Mona e Islote Monito (Mayagüez, 0 residents); Santa Rosa (Utuado, 0 residents). VA, psychiatric and children's hospitals are not counted. Drive time uses the observatory's planning speeds for each class of road (free flow: no traffic, no stops): a rough estimate, shorter than most real trips. The road distance is the firmer figure.
vars.noValue: No road path to a general hospital (an island the roads do not reach, or no road within 2 km)
vars.caution: Which barrios show 0 is uncertain where a hospital is placed at HHS's geocoded address, not at its OpenStreetMap building: HHS's point can fall in another barrio.

vars.group: Health care · Distance to a general hospital
vars.label: Road distance to the nearest general hospital (km)
vars.ref: Computed by the observatory from CMS's hospital list (each hospital placed at its OpenStreetMap building or HHS's geocoded address), the 2020 census blocks and OpenStreetMap roads (conditions.py)
vars.definition: From each barrio's population-weighted point (the 2020 census blocks of the barrio, weighted by their residents) to the nearest general acute care hospital with an emergency department in CMS's Hospital General Information list (37 of the 52 placed at their OpenStreetMap building, found by name or near HHS's geocoded address; 15 at HHS's geocoded address), along the observatory's OpenStreetMap road graph in either direction. A barrio that holds a hospital is 0. Which barrios are 0 is uncertain near the 15 hospitals placed at HHS's address: of the 27 hospitals found by name that HHS also places, HHS's point falls in another barrio for 13. A municipio's figure is the average of its barrios weighted by their 2020 residents. Vieques and Culebra have no road link to a hospital (a trip needs a ferry or a flight), so they have no value, and Puerto Rico's figure leaves out their residents. Other barrios with no value: Isla de Mona e Islote Monito (Mayagüez, 0 residents); Santa Rosa (Utuado, 0 residents). VA, psychiatric and children's hospitals are not counted. An estimate made by the observatory, not a figure CMS publishes.
vars.noValue: No road path to a general hospital (an island the roads do not reach, or no road within 2 km)
vars.caution: Which barrios show 0 is uncertain where a hospital is placed at HHS's geocoded address, not at its OpenStreetMap building: HHS's point can fall in another barrio.

epa_tri.name: EPA — Toxics Release Inventory (TRI), Basic Data File for Puerto Rico
epa_tri.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
epa_tri.note: Facilities that filed a TRI report for the reporting year. The observatory counts them in each barrio and municipio; it publishes no name, address or point.

epa_frs.name: EPA — Facility Registry Service (FRS), Facility Interests (Risk Management Plan facilities, Superfund National Priorities List sites)
epa_frs.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
epa_frs.note: RMP facilities FRS marks active, and NPL sites currently on the final list. The observatory counts them; it publishes no name, address or point.

epa_attains.name: EPA — ATTAINS assessment units (Clean Water Act 303(d) list), Puerto Rico
epa_attains.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
epa_attains.note: Puerto Rico maps its river and stream assessment units as the land that drains to them, so a listed unit covers its watershed, not only the water.

epa_greenbook.name: EPA — Green Book non-attainment areas (lead 2008, sulfur dioxide 2010)
epa_greenbook.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the service states no access or use constraints
epa_greenbook.note: Areas EPA designates as not meeting the national air quality standard for lead or sulfur dioxide.

epa_lmop.name: EPA — Landfill Methane Outreach Program (LMOP), landfills with coordinates
epa_lmop.license: EPA Standard Open Data License: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
epa_lmop.note: Municipal solid waste landfills, open or closed. LMOP does not list every landfill, nor open dumps, transfer stations, industrial or hazardous waste landfills.

hud_chas.name: HUD — Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data by census tract (eGIS)
hud_chas.license: U.S. Public Domain (HUD's open data catalog); HUD adds a disclaimer of warranty and liability
hud_chas.note: A custom tabulation of the American Community Survey that the Census Bureau makes for HUD. The barrio values are the observatory's estimates from the tracts.

census_tiger_lines.name: US Census Bureau — TIGER/Line Shapefiles, all lines (EDGES)
census_tiger_lines.note: The street network the intersections are counted on.

cms_provider_data.name: CMS — Provider Data Catalog (Hospital General Information)
cms_provider_data.note: Acute care hospitals that provide emergency services. Names, addresses and certification numbers are not kept.

hhs_hospital_capacity.name: HHS — COVID-19 Reported Patient Impact and Hospital Capacity by Facility (geocoded hospital addresses)
hhs_hospital_capacity.license: Public Domain U.S. Government (as healthdata.gov states)
hhs_hospital_capacity.note: Used only for the geocoded point of the hospitals OpenStreetMap does not place by name; HHS stopped updating it in May 2024.

osm.name: OpenStreetMap contributors (roads; hospital buildings)
osm.note: The road graph the drive time is measured on (roads.bin), and the building of each hospital whose name OpenStreetMap maps in the same municipio (the observatory's place index, gazetteer.json).

census_tiger.name: US Census Bureau — 2020 census blocks, county subdivisions and land area
census_tiger.note: Barrio outlines, land areas, the 2020 housing units that spread tract counts over barrios, and the residents that weigh each barrio's point.
